tweets.text:
overheard from friends talking about AI in China, and it’s very alarming

- AI short films went massive in China market because of how good the video models are now

- the first wave of people who mastered using AI to generate short films and comics made quite some money because they could produce a lot more content than traditional workflows

- but within just a few months, everybody and their mom could make equally good short films because all the expertise could be written in a markdown file

- when everyone’s more productive, no one actually has an advantage and it’s a race to the bottom. very quickly it became impossible to make money, and everyone’s busier than they were without AI

- the only one making money now is companies like bytedance who owns user demand and distribution. they sell ads to creators who pay to get traffic, and eventually ad spend became 80% of those creators’ operating expense, while AI tokens is less than 5%

so what are the problems here? 

1. there’s no moat if you are creating anything with AI

if a human is really good at something, and it’s hard to find more humans who can do the same, they can leverage the scarcity of their skill to get paid very well

but if AI is good at something, it will be infinitely replicated, so there’s no scarcity hence you can’t really expect a sustainable business by creating anything with AI

2. more creators created more content people actually liked. that’s a good thing

but the economical benefit of that all got absorbed by the distribution platforms

there’s a famous chinese poem 遍身罗绮者，不是养蚕人 - it basically says people who dress well aren’t the people making dresses. that’s exactly what’s happening here

if our society doesn’t figure out a better way to distribute wealth, AI will help billionaires become trillionaires while average people become more exhausted than ever

$USELESS One of the memes that's been most responsive to any bounces on the lower timeframes.

Think this is at a decent level here, right at the Daily 200EMA and been holding up well as most of the market made new lows last week.

If it loses this then the $0.1 region would be next up as support.

These coins are good to trade for their volatility, just make sure you're on the right side of the momentum because when they trend, they trend hard.

I never really short memecoins as they are bound to punish you with random squeezes and such. I do think they can be good directional trades if the market is risk on and you can sit it out for a while to catch a solid move.

Right now, monitoring closely to see if $BTC can lead with some relief and how USELESS reacts.

$BTC and $ETH are on a massive ETF outflow streak.

BTC has seen -$2B in outflows in the past 7 trading days alone.

ETH has also lost about -$1B the past 2 weeks.

Big outflows at local highs/lows can be a sign of absorption or a local reversal area but only if you actually see price stall.

As long as price keeps bleeding as the outflows keep going that just means the selling is adding onto the downside momentum.

When price stalls and outflows keep going, that's when you should be watching closely.

tweets.text:
During times like these it is always interesting to observe how specific events previously seen as bullish narratives, all of the sudden get a bearish outlook instead.

You can see this clearly with the Anthropic IPO these past few weeks.

First valuations keep expanding as the market gets bullish. Then the (arbitrary) number stops going up and doubt starts hitting. This then quickly turns into fear and the idea that the IPO will now just send the entire market into financial disaster.

But keep in mind the market is forward looking. So yes, the initial valuations thrown around some months ago were probably stretched, but the market has also reacted to that by taking out a lot of froth into the main AI names until last week.

Specific events or narratives can turn from bullish to bearish or the other way around quickly based on if price is confirming the people's bias or not.

Just shows you a lot of it is just noise, especially the headlines the media likes throwing around.

But as $BTC & Crypto people we know this all too well. Because we've been declared "dead" hundreds of times by now.

tweets.text:
$BTC Open Interest (in BTC) is back at the highest level we've seen since 2021-2023. 

Every time we hit this area during the past year, we saw a flush of open interest soon after. Usually this was due some sort of squeeze in the market which made the open interest top out.

Keep in mind, this says nothing about which direction that squeeze should be in. But in the majority of the other examples on the chart it did cause a reversal in the market instead of further continuation.

This makes sense as positions tend to build up during a trend. Then when that trend reverses you see those positions cover to take profit or get squeezed out. The other side of the trade generally already got washed out multiple times before.

Next week is going to be interesting as I suspect we will get a resolution on this either way. Eyes on the weekly closes.
